purpose: Decide, without human or LLM judgement, whether a novice-intake slot's value changes parameter compilation. A slot whose value does not change the first compiled calls is defaulted, not asked.

supersedes.why_void: v1 is void, not a finding: 69/72 runs hit the 240s per-run timeout and only 3 isolated signatures were collected; no cell reached two usable repeats sharing a signature, so every slot was INCONCLUSIVE. Full v1 transcripts remain in commit 8d25e5d8.
supersedes.why_this_is_not_a_post_hoc_loosening: v1 produced no usable cell-level signature, so there was nothing to loosen. v2 changes the observation window, not the verdict thresholds: the slot rule and kill criterion are identical to v1 and were frozen before the first v2 run.

inputs.pilots: pilots.json (two mandatory pilot runs, excluded from the 72-cell adjudication)

signature.definition: A run signature is the ordered list of the first 3 distinct tool calls with non-empty args, in order of first appearance. Each call is `tool_name::canonical(args)`. Later calls are execution, not parameter compilation, and are not observed. A run that observed k < 3 calls has a signature of length k. Duplicate emissions of the same canonical call are counted once.

canonical_args.dict: Canonicalise every value, then emit keys sorted by Unicode code point.
canonical_args.list: If every element is a scalar (string, number, boolean, null), sort the canonical JSON text of the elements and canonicalise in that order; otherwise preserve order and canonicalise each element.
canonical_args.string: Strip leading/trailing whitespace. If the result matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:+/-]{1,32}$ (an enum-ish token), lowercase it; otherwise preserve case. Empty-after-strip is preserved as an empty string.
canonical_args.number: Round to 4 decimal places using Python round(); emit as a JSON number so trailing zeros disappear. NaN/Infinity become the strings "nan"/"inf"/"-inf".

signature.signature_serialization: '|'.join(calls) with order preserved and no trailing separator

observation.early_stop: The driver reads the CLI JSON stream line by line and kills the CLI process group as soon as the 3rd distinct non-empty tool call is observed.
observation.timeout_behavior: At 300s the driver kills the CLI process group and preserves every event parsed so far. A run with k>=1 calls is ok_partial; a run with 0 calls is run_error.
observation.natural_completion: A run that exits on its own before 3 calls is ok if k>=1, otherwise run_error.
observation.status_ok: Process exited naturally before the early-stop threshold and observed at least 1 call.
observation.status_ok_partial: Process was stopped early at 3 calls, or was killed at the 300s timeout, and observed at least 1 call. Usable.
observation.status_run_error: No call with non-empty args was observed (timeout, crash, exec failure, or no parseable content).
observation.status_incomplete: The repeat was never started because the batch wall budget was exhausted.
observation.k_calls: Number of distinct calls observed, capped at 3.
observation.killed_by_early_stop: Boolean recorded per run; true only when the 3rd-call threshold triggered the kill.
observation.process_cleanup: After every early stop or timeout the driver calls POST /session/{sessionID}/abort on the lane's host endpoint so the server-side loop does not continue unobserved.
observation.workspace_isolation: Each lane runs one session at a time and clears /workspace/tmp, /workspace/analysis and /workspace/.vt-memory before every run, so no run can compile against another run's artifacts or memories.

run_policy.budget_exhaustion: Repeats that never started are marked incomplete(budget); their cells and slots become INCONCLUSIVE and the verdict states the required-N.
run_policy.retry_policy: A recorded ok, ok_partial or run_error repeat is retained and never replaced. Resume only fills repeats that were never started.
run_policy.pilots: Two pilot runs (market-0 on lane A, risk-0 on lane B, one repeat each) are recorded separately in pilots.json and are excluded from the 72-cell adjudication. The batch proceeds only if each pilot observes at least 1 call in under 120s.

cell_rule.majority_signature: A signature shared by >=2 of the 3 usable repeats. If the 3 usable repeats are all distinct, there is no majority.
cell_rule.stable: A cell is stable iff it has a majority signature and is not INCONCLUSIVE.
cell_rule.inconclusive_if: Fewer than 2 usable repeats, or no signature appears in >=2 repeats.

pair_rule.comparison: For a pair of values (a, b), compare repeat index i = 0,1,2 only where both repeats are usable.
pair_rule.comparable_requirement: At least 2 comparable repeat indices are required for the pair to be evaluable.
pair_rule.differs: The pair differs iff at least 2 comparable repeat indices have different signatures. A pair with fewer than 2 comparable indices is not evaluable and cannot contribute a difference.

precedence: INCONCLUSIVE if >=2 of the slot's 4 cells are INCONCLUSIVE.
default-worthy if all 4 cell majority signatures are identical. A cell with no majority signature cannot satisfy this; the first rule covers the >=2 case.

question-worthy if >=2 distinct majority signatures exist across the slot's 4 values AND at least one value pair differs in >=2 of 3 repeats. A cell without a majority signature contributes no signature but does not by itself block this rule unless the first rule fires.
reported_evidence: per-pair difference counts (comparable repeats) for every value pair
usable repeat count and k-call count per cell

kill_criterion.condition: The count of default-worthy slots is >= 4 of 6.
kill_criterion.consequence: The question-slot table shrinks to private slots only: 成本价 and 仓位规模. The six tested slots (市场, 期限, 风险, 风格, 候选池, 持仓) are defaulted, not asked.
kill_criterion.not_fired_consequence: The question table keeps question-worthy public slots plus private slots 成本价 and 仓位规模; default-worthy public slots are defaulted; INCONCLUSIVE slots are held, not guessed.

output_contract.machine_block: <!-- judge:begin --> ... <!-- judge:end --> containing the JSON per-slot verdicts, stability evidence, v1 evidence summary and kill-criterion outcome
output_contract.tables: Every table row inside verdict.md is emitted by `python judge.py --write`; no hand-copied numbers.
output_contract.check: `python judge.py --check` recomputes every verdict from matrix.json + transcripts/ and exits nonzero on any drift (zero tolerance), including results.json aggregates and the judge_spec.json digest recorded at run time.
output_contract.v1_evidence_table: verdict.md includes a table summarising v1_evidence/results.json: runs, signatures, cell-level majorities, and why v1 was void.

pre_registration.digest_rule: sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes of judge_spec.json exactly as committed. The runner records this digest in results.json meta.judge_spec_sha256 before the first v2 run; judge.py recomputes it and refuses to judge on mismatch.
pre_registration.threshold_change_policy: Thresholds and the slot rule may not be loosened after seeing v2 results. Any edit to this file after the first v2 run voids v2 and requires redoing all 72 sessions.
